chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: Invitations to sing again and the Dick Gibson jazz party
summary: She was not ready to stop work and then got invitations that led back to performing with a good reception.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: time and I wasn't ready to stop. But later on I got an invitation to go out to Denver, Colorado to do the Gibson Jazz party. And this was the annual party that Dick has and he invites alot of musicians out there. I ran into musicians I hadn't seen for years because I hadn't been active.

And so I got a very good reception and it was during this time that Dick Gibson formed - ten of the guys were there, Bob Haggart Mank Lawson, Bob Wilber and some of the rest and they formed the World's Greatest Jazz Band. Well in 1968 Dick Gibson brought the boys to open at the River Boat in New York. I didn't go into the River Boat with the Worlds Greatest Jazz Band but toward the end of their engagement which must have been around the end of December, I happened to go down to the River Boat to catch the band and to say hello to the boys and Bobby Hackett was in the audience. And he said that he was opening in the River Boat on January 3rd, of 1969 and wanted to know If I'd go in with him. So I decided I would go in with him. So this had to be the end of my work at the school because I was going to be tied up. I stayed a little longer. I got involved in a program

at the school called The Urban Rural School Development Program. It was a program to train teachers and para-professionals and even local community people to become more involved in the education of the kids in school. And I did a few things with the Worlds Greatest Jazz Band and after I left the River Boat with Bobby, and then they decided they were going to do this tour abroad I had to leave the system because this meant that I would be out of the Country and I had to give it up.
